sources.title: Exergame and Balance Training Modulate Prefrontal Brain Activity during Walking and Enhance Executive Function in Older Adults
sources.authors: Eggenberger P, Wolf M, Schumann M, de Bruin ED.

sources.title: Does multicomponent physical exercise with simultaneous cognitive training boost cognitive performance in older adults? A 6-month randomized controlled trial with a 1-year follow-up
sources.authors: Eggenberger P, Schumacher V, Angst M, Theill N, de Bruin ED.

findings.finding: Physical exercise interventions effectively reduce the rate of falls in older adults living in the community.
findings.quote: Exercise reduces the rate of falls by 23% (pooled rate ratio (RaR) 0.77, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.71 to 0.83, 64 studies, high certainty evidence).

findings.finding: Three-dimensional exercise interventions, including dance and yoga, demonstrate improvements in balance measures such as single-leg stance and Timed Up & Go test scores.
findings.quote: 3D (3 dimensional) exercise (including Tai Chi, qi gong, dance, yoga) (15 studies of which seven provided primary outcome data): Timed Up & Go Test

findings.finding: Interactive video game dancing combined with balance training modulates prefrontal brain activity during walking and enhances cognitive executive functions.
findings.quote: Both interventions significantly reduced left and right hemispheric PFC oxygenation during the acceleration of walking (p < 0.05 or trend, r = 0.25-0.36), while DANCE showed a larger reduction at the end of the 30-s walking task compared to BALANCE in the left PFC

findings.finding: Simultaneous cognitive-physical training programs like video game dancing provide added benefits in dimensions of executive function compared to exclusively physical training.
findings.quote: Advantages of the simultaneous cognitive-physical programs were found in two dimensions of executive function.

principle: Exercise interventions incorporating physical and cognitive components can improve balance, reduce falls, and enhance executive functions and brain plasticity in older adults.
for_the_teacher: Include balance challenges and single-leg standing tasks into lessons to support stability and fall prevention.
Combine simultaneous cognitive tasks, such as memory or attention cues, with physical steps to engage executive functions.
